title: Training in the Pharmacological Sciences
text: The UVA Pharmacological Sciences Training Program (PSTP) teaches talented scientists to apply innovative approaches to pressing biomedical problems using Pharmacologic methods. Our graduates are poised to become the next generation of leaders in academia, government and the pharmaceutical industry.

title: Investigating the Role of Histamine and HRH1 in Mucus Secretion in the Salivary Glands
text:
Salivary glands harbor the histamine receptor HRH1; but little is known about the role of histamine and HRH1
signaling in salivary gland mucus secretion and maintenance of oral health. This proposal aims to elucidate the
role of histamine in stimulating mucus secretion and to evaluate the effects of histamine-producing probiotics on
salivary glands. This work has the potential to identify new targets for therapeutics to improve oral health.

title: Broad Institute Mendelian Genomic Research Center
text:
This administrative supplement will enable cross-consortium harmonization and joint analysis of long-read
genome sequencing (lrGS), structural variation (SV), and multiomic data generated by GREGoR. Our Center
will perform additional analyses and provide additional resources to support the GREGoR consortium. This will
include enhancements to the seqr analysis platform to support analysis and data sharing within and external to
the consortium.

title: Bioinformatics and Biotechnology Shared Resource (BBSR)
text: BIOINFORMATICS AND BIOTECHNOLOGY SHARED RESOURCE The goal of the Bioinformatics and Biotechnology Shared Resource (BBSR) is to provide the latest innovative, high-throughput biotechnology as well as bioinformatics methods and workflows to support the research of the St. Jude Comprehensive Cancer Center (SJCCC) members. The Biotechnology team provides state-of-the-art high-throughput genomic assays of RNA and DNA samples by using complementary platforms: short- and long- read genome sequencing, Sanger sequencing, short tandem–repeat profiling, and microarray analysis. The Bioinformatics team provides customized and/or advanced data analyses using on-premises and cloud-based high-performance computing infrastructure with graphics processing unit-accelerated algorithms. The BBSR is directed by Gang Wu, PhD, who has over 18 years’ experience in bioinformatics and genomics research. Wu specializes in developing novel methods to analyze complex genomic lesions and how rare germline variants could contribute to human disease predisposition. This shared resource is codirected by Geoffrey Neale, PhD, who has over 25 years’ experience in scientific management and the molecular investigation of pediatric cancers. Both Wu and Neale have been among the top 1% highly cited researchers in immunology recent years. The BBSR has 41 institution-funded staff, including 22 PhD-level scientists with various specializations and domain knowledge. Services include technical and analytical support for state-of-the-art molecular profiling (e.g. next- generation sequencing, microarrays, single-cell sequencing, and spatial biology analysis). Professional consultancy, advisory support, hands-on training, and bioinformatics data analyses are free of charge. The impact of the BBSR on SJCCC research is evidenced by the significant contribution to grant applications and scientific publications, many in high-impact journals (impact factor >10), such as the Nature Medicine, Nature, Cell, Journal of Clinical Oncology, and Science. During the project period, the BBSR supported all five SJCCC Programs, resulting in 577 publications, 232 (40.21%) of which were from interprogrammatic studies, demonstrating the high level of collaborative research enabled by the BBSR. Furthermore, 327 (56.67%) Additionally, BBSR staff have prominent authorships on 22 publications. The BBSR was used by 85 SJCCC members, representing 56% of all PIs supported (152 total users). During the next project period, the BBSR will continue evaluating newly developed technologies and published analytical methods to address the needs of SJCCC members. The BBSR will also continue to collaborate with the SJCCC Programs to establish novel bioinformatics methods in pan-genome analysis, long-read technologies (PacBio and Oxford Nanopore), single cell and spatial omics, as well as multiomics/multimodality integration. Finally, the BBSR will continue developing artificial intelligence-powered methods and workflows on local high-performance computers and in multicloud environments to support data scientists in the SJCCC and throughout the world by providing direct access to complex bioinformatics workflows.

title: The changing landscape of work in the United States and stalling life expectancy improvements
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Despite the established understanding that paid work is an important determinant of health, demographic
research on stalled U.S. life expectancy improvements has not systematically evaluated the role of work in
shaping population mortality trends. In this K01, Dr. Abrams will use innovative data linkages to identify how
changing mortality rates within occupations and changing distributions of occupations across the population
have contributed to mortality trends in recent decades, as well as which working conditions explain excess
cause-specific mortality in high-risk occupations. Supported by expert mentorship and training in occupational
epidemiology, data science, and research translation, the proposed research will put forward new healthrelevant
groups of occupations to be utilized by future research and will contribute novel evidence to inform
practices that protect workforce health.

title: Limiting RNA pseudouridylation to treat adverse cardiac remodeling and heart failure
text:
Heart failure affects over 6 million Americans and remains a leading cause of death, with nearly half of patients
dying within 5 years of diagnosis despite current treatments. Our research has discovered that blocking a speciﬁc
enzyme called PUS7 can protect heart cells from damage and prevent the formation of harmful scar tissue that
makes the heart pump less effectively. The main goal of this proposal is to develop new medications targeting
PUS7 that could prevent heart failure progression, ultimately improving quality of life and saving lives for millions
of patients with heart disease.

title: Novel statistical genetics methods to unravel polygenic interactions in complex traits
text: Although genetic studies of complex traits have found many trait-associated loci, they rarely reveal new biology and they yield suboptimal genetic predictions. Studies of interactions between genes (GxG) or between genes and the environment (GxE) have potential to address these limitations, but current models are unrealistic and underpowered. I will develop new rigorous models of GxG and GxE and apply them in across several large-scale datasets and traits that range from single cell ‘omics to asthma in order to better understand complex trait biology and to improve accuracy in genetic medicine.

title: Wirelessly Actuated Ciliary Stent for Minimally Invasive Treatment of Cilia Dysfunction
text:
Our proposed implantable airway stents with integrated artificial cilia, overcome the limitation of existing airway
stents such as tissue ingrowth or cilia impairment, and can allow minimally invasive removal of excessive mucus
in the airway. It thus addresses the current limitation of existing airway stents in terms of excessive accumulation
of mucus in patients with Central Airway Obstruction due to Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and other
lung diseases. The proposed work thus could lead to novel implantable medical devices which can save lives and
improve the quality of our life, with an eventual goal to shed light on new therapies for pulmonary diseases and
other diseases related to cilia dysfunction.

title: Core A: Biostatistics and Computational Biology Core
text: (CORE A, BIOSTATISTICS AND COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY CORE) The Biostatistics and Computational Biology (BCB) Core provides comprehensive professional support to ensure statistical integrity, including study design, algorithm selection and implementation, data integrity across the entire research cycle, internal and external data sharing, and data analysis/interpretation of the studies performed by the University of Michigan SPORE titled Molecularly Targeted Radiosensitization of Locally Advanced Cancers. The Core assists investigators with the proper planning of experiments and choice of technologies, assists with the information management of laboratory-based experimental and clinical data generated by SPORE projects, and conducts rigorous biostatistical and bioinformatics analyses in close collaboration with the SPORE investigators. The BCB Core includes members with diverse expertise and experience. The core leaders, Drs. Schipper and Rao, are assisted by faculty and staff analysts and programmers with the expertise needed to support the activities in the SPORE. The core will support data flow and warehousing within the SPORE as well as with entities outside of the SPORE. Both leaders are integrated into the biostatistical and bioinformatic infrastructures at the University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center, and they can call on additional assistance as needed to support the evolving research of the SPORE. The Core has the flexibility to match personnel to the needs of existing and developmental SPORE projects.

title: Impact of State Cannabis Laws on Cancer Pain Management and Outcomes: A mixed-methods study
text:
The proposed study fills a major gap in knowledge about how state medical and adult-use (i.e., recreational)
cannabis laws have impacted opioid receipt and pain outcomes in cancer. We will triangulate findings from a
quantitative policy evaluation with information from surveys and interviews that explore cancer centers’
implementation of state cannabis laws, physicians’ practices for recommending, and patients’ practices for
using cannabis for cancer pain. To inform a rapidly evolving policy landscape—in which states are
continuously considering, enacting, or expanding cannabis laws— it is essential to understand how these laws
affect pain management practices and outcomes for patients with cancer as one of the largest groups of
consumers of therapeutic cannabis.

title: Phenotypic and biological features of mucus plugs in asthma
text:
We hypothesize that airway mucus plugs are an under-appreciated cause of airflow obstruction in severe forms
of asthma and that muco-active treatment in mucus plug-high asthma will improve airflow in these patients. We
further hypothesize that intelectin has a pivotal role in mediating airway mucus plug formation in asthma.

title: Synaptic protein composition and localization in individuals with schizophrenia
text:
Schizophrenia is a chronic illness with no treatments that interfere with the disease process. To
design treatments that will change the course of schizophrenia illness, we need to map the
detailed ways in which brains of people with schizophrenia differ. In this project, a new imaging
method will be used to test whether there is an abnormality in the number of specific types of
connection points between neurons in the brains of people with schizophrenia.

title: Reduction of Intracochlear Trauma and Fibrosis Using Dual Network, Zwitterionic Hydrogel Thin Films on Cochlear Implant Surfaces
text:
Cochlear implants represent the most successful neuroprosthesis in clinical use, providing
direct electrical stimulation to the auditory nerve to restore hearing to deaf patients. However, cochlear implant
recipients usually struggle to understand complex auditory signals such as speech in noise and music. These
studies seek to develop and understand novel thin film coatings applied to the implant to diminish trauma and
scarring in the cochlea, improve the interface of the implant with the cochlear tissues, and enhance the ability
of cochlear implants to represent complex auditory signals.

title: Long-Lived Cardiac Myosins as Regulators of Oocyte Cytoskeletal Integrity and Reproductive Lifespan
text:
Age-related decline in oocyte quality is a major cause of infertility, pregnancy loss, and chromosomal disorders,
yet the mechanisms that safeguard oocyte health during the decades-long pause before ovulation remain
unclear. This project will define how exceptionally long-lived cardiac cytoskeletal proteins preserve oocyte
structure and function with age, challenging current views of cytoskeletal maintenance in the female germline.
By defining how these long-lived proteins support oocyte quality and testing strategies to enhance their function
in aged oocytes, this work could inform novel approaches to protect fertility and improve reproductive health
outcomes in women.

title: Exploring Mechanisms in Retinal Development/Homeostasis, Retinal Immune Surveillance and Diabetic Retinopathy Using Forward Genetics
text:
A functioning retina is the result of an extraordinary orchestration of complex pathways responsible for its
development and homeostasis; any deficits in these pathways may lead to disease and loss of sight. We have
recently shown that a powerful and unbiased state-of-the-science forward genetics approach can be used to
identify novel gene-phenotype associations that are crucial to retinal health, and we propose now to exploit this
strategy to identify and characterize genes and pathways that regulate: 1) retinal development and homeostasis,
2) retinal immune surveillance, and 3) early diabetic retinopathy. Our long-term goal is to leverage our research
results for the discovery of novel therapeutic targets for retinal diseases and in the development of new retinal
regeneration strategies.

title: Viral and Host Determinants of Infant and Childhood Allergy and Asthma
text:
OVERALL PROGRAM – NARRATIVE
The focus of this application is on the diseased organ in asthma, the airway, answering key questions to
support the rational development of biologically targeted asthma prevention and treatment strategies. Project 1
aims to understand the development of the airway epithelium in health and asthma, and how early life RSV
infection alters development using longitudinal samples from a novel birth cohort study and multi-omic
analyses. Project 2 similarly focuses on the developing airway epithelium, using an airway epithelial cell culture
model with samples collected from infants longitudinally beginning at birth to understand differentiation in vitro
and assess the impact of early life RSV infection on airway development to understand the enhanced
susceptibility of asthmatics and asthmatic airway epithelium to respiratory viral infection.

title: BCG-Mediated Immunotherapy Against Bacteria
text:
Relevance Statement
Bladder infections are a significant medical problem because of its high rate of recurrence, an
attribute related to bacterial persistence in the bladder long after infection has resolved. We
have recently discovered that intravesical administration of a vaccine formulation that includes
the live attenuated vaccine, Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG), is highly effective in eliminating
bacteria harboring in the bladder. Here, we propose to demonstrate the efficacy and durability
of this novel immunotherapy when applied alone and in combination with vaccine antigens and
to explore its underling basis of action.

title: Skin probiotics to treat atopic dermatitis
text:
Atopic dermatitis (AD) is characterized by a defective skin barrier primarily compromised
by protease activity. This project focuses on a multi-pronged protease inhibitor therapy,
produced continuously by genetically engineered bacteria, tested in a protease-driven AD
murine model. Success in this approach will lead to an IND application and offer a new, targeted
treatment paradigm for AD, addressing the condition at its proteolytic core.

title: Genetics-based discovery of novel genes regulating follicular helper T cell function
text:
This proposal is focused on follicular helper T cells, an immune cell type that is crucial for the generation of high-
affinity, class-switched antibodies that mediate immunity to pathogens, but also contributes to antibody-mediated
diseases like allergy, organ transplant rejection, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
Genome-wide association studies show that susceptibility to antibody-mediated disease has a strong genetic
component, and the underlying hypothesis of the proposal is that these genetics hold clues to how all T cell-
dependent B cell antibody responses are regulated. Our major goal is to use sophisticated analytical and
experimental approaches to interpret these genetic cues and power the discovery of novel genes and
immunomodulatory mechanisms underlying humoral immunity and systemic autoimmune disease.

title: The RESILIENT Brace: a flexible, adjustable, connected bracing system for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis
text:
Every year, more than 12,000 children in the US are diagnosed with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (IS) and
require bracing; without treatment, their spinal curvature can progress to the point it requires invasive and costly
spinal fusion surgery, which costs the healthcare system hundreds of millions of dollars annually. Yet because
the current standard of care is for patients to wear a rigid brace that is painful, immobilizing, and––above all––
conspicuous to their adolescent peers, up to half of patients either fail to wear their brace or wear it for an
inadequate period or at an insufficient force to correct their spinal curve. To achieve better patient compliance,
Thinks Works is developing an innovative, low-profile (similar to a hydration pack) bracing system that incorpo-
rates force sensors to help patients apply the proper force for treatment and track wear time; the proposed project
will finalize aspects of the design and collect preliminary user feedback to prepare for an exploratory clinical trial
of the brace's efficacy.
